entries.definition: Anchovies are small, common forage fish of the family Engraulidae.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Anchovy”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Anchovies (family Engraulidae)
facts.habitat: Warm and temperate seas worldwide, in big schools near the surface
facts.food: Plankton
facts.size: Up to 40 cm, most under 20 cm

entries.definition: Marine angelfish are perciform fish of the family Pomacanthidae.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Pomacanthidae”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Marine angelfish (family Pomacanthidae)
facts.habitat: Shallow tropical coral reefs
facts.food: Sponges, algae and small sea creatures
facts.size: Up to 60 cm, most much smaller

entries.definition: The anglerfish are ray-finned fish in the order Lophiiformes.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Anglerfish”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Anglerfish (order Lophiiformes)
facts.habitat: Seas worldwide, many in the deep dark ocean
facts.food: Fish and other prey, lured close by a glowing or wiggling lure on its head

entries.definition: The arapaima, pirarucu, or paiche is a large species of bonytongue in the genus Arapaima native to the Amazon and Essequibo basins of South America.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Arapaima”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Arapaima (Arapaima gigas)
facts.habitat: Rivers and flooded forests of the Amazon basin
facts.food: Fish, plus crabs, fruit, seeds, insects and small animals near the shore

entries.definition: Osteoglossinae are a subfamily of freshwater bony fish, commonly known as arowanas or bonytongues (though the latter is also used for other osteoglossiform fish).
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Arowana”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Arowanas (subfamily Osteoglossinae)
facts.habitat: Slow rivers and swamps in South America, Asia and Australia
facts.food: Insects, small fish and even birds, leaping out of the water to catch them
facts.size: Up to 90 cm in the silver arowana

entries.definition: Asian carp is a term that groups together several species of carp native to Eurasia, commonly referring to the four East Asian species silver carp, bighead carp, grass carp (or white amur) and black carp (or black amur), which were introduced to North America during the 1970s and are now regarded as invasive in the United States.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Asian carp”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Asian carp (silver, bighead, grass and black carp)
facts.habitat: Large rivers and lakes; native to East Asia, invasive in North America
facts.food: Plankton or water plants, depending on the kind
facts.size: Big — a black carp can weigh 70 kg

entries.definition: Barbels are a group of carp-like freshwater fish, almost all of the genus Barbus.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Barbel (fish)”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Common barbel (Barbus barbus)
facts.habitat: Fast, clear rivers in Europe
facts.food: Small animals from the riverbed, like insect larvae, snails and shrimp, plus small fish
facts.size: Up to 1.2 m, usually around 30 cm

entries.definition: A barracuda is a large, predatory, ray-finned, saltwater fish of the genus Sphyraena, the only genus in the family Sphyraenidae, which was named by Constantine Samuel Rafinesque in 1815.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Barracuda”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Barracudas (genus Sphyraena)
facts.habitat: Warm seas worldwide, near reefs and the surface
facts.food: Fish

entries.definition: Basa (Pangasius bocourti), as it is commonly referred to, is a species of primarily freshwater-dwelling catfish in the shark-catfish family, Pangasiidae, native to the Mekong and Chao Phraya river basins of Mainland Southeast Asia.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Basa (fish)”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Basa (Pangasius bocourti)
facts.habitat: Big rivers of Southeast Asia, especially the Mekong
facts.food: Mostly plants

entries.definition: Bass is a common name shared by many species of ray-finned fish from the large clade Percomorpha, mainly belonging to the orders Perciformes and Moroniformes, encompassing both freshwater and marine species.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Bass (fish)”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Bass (many kinds, from sea bass to black bass)
facts.habitat: Seas, rivers and lakes worldwide, depending on the kind
facts.food: Varies between kinds

entries.definition: Blue tang is the common name of several species of surgeonfish.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Blue tang”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Pacific blue tang (Paracanthurus hepatus)
facts.habitat: Coral reefs of the Indian and Pacific oceans
facts.food: Plankton, and sometimes algae

entries.definition: The bluegill (Lepomis macrochirus), sometimes referred to as "bream", "brim", "sunny", or, in Texas, "copper nose", is a species of North American freshwater fish, native to and commonly found in streams, rivers, lakes, ponds and wetlands east of the Rocky Mountains.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Bluegill”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Bluegill (Lepomis macrochirus)
facts.habitat: Lakes, ponds and slow streams in North America
facts.food: Insects, worms and small fish
facts.size: Up to 40 cm, usually under 30 cm

entries.definition: The ruddy bowfin (Amia calva) is a ray-finned fish native to North America.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Bowfin”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Bowfin (Amia calva)
facts.habitat: Swamps, lakes and slow rivers in eastern North America
facts.food: Fish, crayfish and frogs

entries.definition: Bream are species of freshwater fish belonging to a variety of genera including Abramis (e.g., A. brama, the common bream), Ballerus, Blicca, Chilotilapia, Etelis, Lepomis, Gymnocranius, Lethrinus, Nemipterus, Pharyngochromis, Rhabdosargus, Scolopsis, or Serranochromis.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Bream”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Common bream (Abramis brama)
facts.habitat: Lakes, slow rivers and estuaries in Europe
facts.food: Insects, small crustaceans, snails and plants; big ones eat small fish
facts.size: Up to 82 cm, usually around 25 cm

entries.definition: The cabezon (Scorpaenichthys marmoratus) is a large species of sculpin native to the Pacific coast of North America.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Cabezon (fish)”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Cabezon (Scorpaenichthys marmoratus)
facts.habitat: Rocky reefs and kelp forests along North America's Pacific coast
facts.food: Crabs, small fish and shellfish

entries.definition: The term carp is a generic common name for numerous species of freshwater fish from the family Cyprinidae, a very large clade of ray-finned fish mostly native to Eurasia.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Carp”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Common carp (Cyprinus carpio)
facts.habitat: Lakes, ponds and slow rivers worldwide
facts.food: Small animals from the bottom, and plants

entries.definition: Catfish are a diverse group of ray-finned fish of the order Siluriformes (historically Nematognathi).
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Catfish”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Catfish (order Siluriformes)
facts.habitat: Fresh water on every continent but Antarctica; a few live in the sea
facts.food: Mostly food from the bottom, found with the whiskers around their mouths

entries.definition: Squalius cephalus, the common chub, European chub or simply chub, is a species of freshwater ray-finned fish belonging to the family Leuciscidae, the daces, Eurasian minnows and related fishes.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Squalius cephalus”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Common chub (Squalius cephalus)
facts.habitat: Rivers and streams across Europe
facts.food: Insects, worms, small fish and berries
facts.size: Up to 60 cm, most around 30 cm

entries.definition: Clownfish or anemonefishes (genus Amphiprion) are saltwater fish found in the warm and tropical waters of the Indo-Pacific.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Clownfish”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Clownfish (genus Amphiprion)
facts.habitat: Warm coral reefs, living among the stinging arms of sea anemones
facts.food: Plankton, algae and small sea creatures

entries.definition: The cobia (Rachycentron canadum) is a species of marine carangiform ray-finned fish, the only extant representative of the genus Rachycentron and the family Rachycentridae.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Cobia”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Cobia (Rachycentron canadum)
facts.habitat: Warm seas worldwide, often around floating objects and reefs
facts.food: Crabs, squid and fish

entries.definition: Cod is the common name for the demersal fish genus Gadus, belonging to the family Gadidae.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Cod”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Atlantic cod (Gadus morhua)
facts.habitat: Cold waters of the North Atlantic
facts.food: Fish, crabs and worms
facts.size: Up to 2 m, usually under 1 m

entries.definition: Corydoras is a genus of freshwater ray-finned fish belonging to the family Callichthyidae, commonly referred to as the armoured catfishes, and the subfamily Corydoradinae, the corys.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Corydoras”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Corydoras catfish (genus Corydoras)
facts.habitat: Shallow streams and pools in South America
facts.lifespan: Up to 20 years in an aquarium
facts.food: Worms, insect larvae and bits of plants from the bottom
facts.size: Up to 12 cm, most around 5 cm

entries.definition: The Atlantic croaker (Micropogonias undulatus) is a species of marine ray-finned fish belonging to the family Sciaenidae and is closely related to the black drum (Pogonias cromis), the silver perch (Bairdiella chrysoura), the spot croaker (Leiostomus xanthurus), the red drum (Sciaenops ocellatus), the spotted seatrout (Cynoscion nebulosus), and the weakfish (Cynoscion regalis).
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Atlantic croaker”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Atlantic croaker (Micropogonias undulatus)
facts.habitat: Coasts and river mouths of the western Atlantic
facts.food: Worms, shrimp, crabs and small fish
facts.size: Up to 70 cm, usually under 50 cm

entries.definition: The common dab (Limanda limanda) is an edible flatfish of the family Pleuronectidae.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Common dab”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Common dab (Limanda limanda)
facts.habitat: Sandy seabeds of the northeast Atlantic
facts.food: Worms, shrimp and other small seabed animals

entries.definition: Damselfish are fish within the subfamilies Abudefdufinae, Chrominae, Lepidozyginae, Pomacentrinae, and Stegastinae within the family Pomacentridae.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Damselfish”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Damselfish (family Pomacentridae)
facts.habitat: Warm coral reefs worldwide
facts.food: Algae and plankton
facts.size: Up to 30 cm, most much smaller

entries.definition: The mahi-mahi, common dolphinfish, dolphinfish, dolphin or dorado (Coryphaena hippurus) is a surface-dwelling ray-finned fish found in off-shore temperate, tropical, and subtropical waters worldwide.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Mahi-mahi”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Mahi-mahi (Coryphaena hippurus)
facts.habitat: Open warm seas worldwide, near the surface
facts.food: Flying fish, squid and other fish

entries.definition: John Dory, St Pierre, or Peter's fish are names which refers to fish of the genus Zeus, especially Zeus faber, which is a demersal coastal marine fish.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “John Dory”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: John Dory (Zeus faber)
facts.habitat: Coastal seas of Europe, Africa, Asia and Australia
facts.food: Small fish, crept up on from the front

entries.definition: Sciaenidae is a family of ray-finned fishes belonging to the order Acanthuriformes.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Sciaenidae”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Drums and croakers (family Sciaenidae)
facts.habitat: Coasts, river mouths and some rivers worldwide
facts.food: Shrimp, crabs and fish

entries.definition: Eels are ray-finned fish belonging to the order Anguilliformes, which consists of eight suborders, 20 families, 164 genera, and about 1000 species.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Eel”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Eels (order Anguilliformes)
facts.habitat: Seas worldwide; some, like the European eel, live in rivers
facts.food: Mostly other animals — most eels are hunters

entries.definition: Flounders are a group of flatfish species.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Flounder”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Flounders (several families of flatfish)
facts.habitat: Sandy seabeds and river mouths
facts.food: Worms, shrimp and small fish
facts.size: Up to 95 cm, most under 60 cm

entries.definition: The Exocoetidae are a family of saltwater ray-finned fish in the order Beloniformes, known colloquially as flying fish or flying cod, with about 64 species in seven genera.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Flying fish”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Flying fish (family Exocoetidae)
facts.habitat: Warm open seas, near the surface
facts.food: Plankton

entries.definition: The giant trevally (Caranx ignobilis), also known as the lowly trevally, barrier trevally, giant kingfish, or ulua, is a species of large marine fish classified in the jack family, Carangidae.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Giant trevally”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Giant trevally (Caranx ignobilis)
facts.habitat: Reefs and coasts of the Indian and Pacific oceans
facts.food: Fish, squid and crabs

entries.definition: The goblin shark (Mitsukurina owstoni) is a rare species of deep-sea shark.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Goblin shark”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Goblin shark (Mitsukurina owstoni)
facts.habitat: The deep sea worldwide, below 100 m
facts.food: Deep-sea fish, octopus and crabs, snatched with jaws that shoot forward
facts.size: Up to 6 m, usually around 3 m

entries.definition: The Gobioidei are a suborder of percomorph fish.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Gobioidei”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Gobies (suborder Gobioidei)
facts.habitat: Seas, river mouths and fresh water worldwide
facts.food: Small animals and algae

entries.definition: The California golden trout (Oncorhynchus aguabonita) is a species of trout native to California.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Golden trout”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: California golden trout (Oncorhynchus aguabonita)
facts.habitat: Cold high mountain streams and lakes in California
facts.food: Not well known

entries.definition: The goldfish (Carassius auratus) is a freshwater fish in the family Cyprinidae of the order Cypriniformes.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Goldfish”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Goldfish (Carassius auratus)
facts.habitat: Ponds and aquariums worldwide; first bred in China
facts.food: Plankton, small bottom animals and plants
facts.size: Up to 48 cm, usually around 10 cm

entries.definition: Thymallus thymallus, harjus, the grayling or European grayling, is a species of freshwater fish in the salmon family Salmonidae.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Thymallus thymallus”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Grayling (Thymallus thymallus)
facts.habitat: Cold, clean rivers in Europe
facts.food: Insects, shrimp, snails and small fish

entries.definition: Groupers are a diverse group of marine ray-finned fish in the family Epinephelidae, in the order Perciformes.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Grouper”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Groupers (family Epinephelidae)
facts.habitat: Warm seas worldwide, around reefs and rocks
facts.food: Fish, crabs and octopus, swallowed whole

entries.definition: Gobio gobio, or the gudgeon or common gudgeon, is a species of fish in the family Gobionidae.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Gobio gobio”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Gudgeon (Gobio gobio)
facts.habitat: Rivers and lakes across Europe
facts.food: Insect larvae, worms and snails from the bottom
facts.size: Up to 20 cm, usually around 12 cm

entries.definition: The guppy (Poecilia reticulata), also known as the millionfish or rainbow fish, is a member of the family Poeciliidae and, akin to most New World members of the family, is classified as a livebearer.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Guppy”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Guppy (Poecilia reticulata)
facts.habitat: Streams and pools in northern South America; aquariums worldwide
facts.food: Algae, insects and fish food

entries.definition: Triglidae, commonly known as gurnards or sea robins, are a family of bottom-feeding scorpaenoid ray-finned fish.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Triglidae”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Gurnards (family Triglidae)
facts.habitat: Sandy and muddy seabeds worldwide
facts.food: Shrimp, crabs and small fish, found by 'walking' on finger-like fins

entries.definition: The haddock (Melanogrammus aeglefinus) is a saltwater ray-finned fish from the family Gadidae, the true cods.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Haddock”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Haddock (Melanogrammus aeglefinus)
facts.habitat: Cold waters of the North Atlantic
facts.food: Worms, shellfish, starfish and small fish
facts.size: Up to 94 cm, usually 30 to 70 cm

entries.definition: Hake is the common name for fish in the Merlucciidae family of the northern and southern oceans and the Phycidae family of the northern oceans.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Hake”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Hake (family Merlucciidae)
facts.habitat: Deep coastal seas worldwide
facts.food: Fish and squid, near the seabed

entries.definition: Halibut is the common name for three species of flatfish in the family of right-eye flounders.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Halibut”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Atlantic halibut (Hippoglossus hippoglossus)
facts.habitat: Cold northern seas, on the seabed
facts.food: Fish, crabs and squid
facts.size: Up to 4.7 m — the biggest flatfish

entries.definition: The hammerhead sharks are a group of sharks that form the family Sphyrnidae, named for the unusual and distinctive form of their heads, which are flattened and laterally extended into a cephalofoil (a T-shape or "hammer").
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Hammerhead shark”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Hammerhead sharks (family Sphyrnidae)
facts.habitat: Warm coasts worldwide
facts.food: Fish, squid and stingrays

entries.definition: Herring are various species of forage fish, belonging to the order Clupeiformes.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Herring”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Atlantic herring (Clupea harengus)
facts.habitat: Cold northern seas, in huge schools
facts.food: Plankton

entries.definition: The king mackerel (Scomberomorus cavalla), kingfish or carite lucio is a migratory species of mackerel of the western Atlantic Ocean and Gulf of Mexico.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “King mackerel”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: King mackerel (Scomberomorus cavalla)
facts.habitat: Warm western Atlantic and the Gulf of Mexico
facts.food: Fish, plus some shrimp and squid

entries.definition: Koi (Japanese: 鯉; Japanese: [koꜜi], literally 'carp'), or more specifically nishikigoi (錦鯉; Japanese: [ɲiɕi̥kiꜜɡoi], literally 'brocaded carp'), are colored varieties of carp (Cyprinus sp.) that are kept for decorative purposes in outdoor koi ponds or water gardens.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Koi”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Koi (Cyprinus rubrofuscus)
facts.habitat: Garden ponds worldwide; first bred in Japan
facts.food: Plants, insects and fish food

entries.definition: Lampreys (sometimes inaccurately called lamprey eels) are a group of jawless fish composing the order Petromyzontiformes, sole order in the class Petromyzontida.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Lamprey”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Lampreys (order Petromyzontiformes)
facts.habitat: Rivers and seas in cool parts of the world
facts.lifespan: Varies between kinds — most of it is spent as a larva
facts.food: Blood and flesh of other fish, sucked through a round toothed mouth

entries.definition: The lemon shark (Negaprion brevirostris) is a species of requiem shark from the family Carcharhinidae, known for its yellowish skin, which inspires its common name.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Lemon shark”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Lemon shark (Negaprion brevirostris)
facts.habitat: Shallow warm coasts and mangroves of the Atlantic and eastern Pacific
facts.food: Mostly fish, found at night by sensing their electric signals

entries.definition: Lionfish are venomous marine ray-finned fish of the genus Pterois, native to coral reefs of the Indo-Pacific.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Lionfish”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Lionfish (genus Pterois)
facts.habitat: Coral reefs of the Indian and Pacific oceans; invasive in the Atlantic
facts.food: Small fish and shrimp
facts.size: Up to 46 cm in the red lionfish

entries.definition: Mackerel is a common name applied to a number of different species of pelagic fish, mostly from the family Scombridae.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Mackerel”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Atlantic mackerel (Scomber scombrus)
facts.habitat: Open seas of the North Atlantic, in big schools
facts.food: Plankton and small fish

entries.definition: Manta rays are large rays belonging to the genus Mobula (formerly its own genus Manta).
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Manta ray”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Manta rays (genus Mobula)
facts.habitat: Warm open seas worldwide
facts.food: Plankton, filtered from the water

entries.definition: Marlins are fish from the family Istiophoridae, which includes between 9 and 11 species, depending on the taxonomic authority.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Marlin”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Marlins (family Istiophoridae)
facts.habitat: Warm open seas worldwide
facts.food: Other sea animals — marlins are top predators

entries.definition: Minnow is the common name for a number of species of small freshwater fish, belonging to several genera of the family Cyprinidae and in particular the subfamily Leuciscinae.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Minnow”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Eurasian minnow (Phoxinus phoxinus)
facts.habitat: Cold, clean streams, rivers and lakes across Europe and northern Asia
facts.food: Algae, plants, snails, tiny crustaceans and insects
facts.size: Up to 14 cm, usually around 7 cm

entries.definition: The sailfin molly (Poecilia latipinna) is a livebearer fish typically found in both freshwater and brackish waterways along the East Coast of the United States, from North Carolina south to Florida, and around the Gulf of Mexico to Texas, and south to the Yucatán Peninsula of Mexico.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Sailfin molly”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Sailfin molly (Poecilia latipinna)
facts.habitat: Fresh and brackish water in the southern United States and Mexico; aquariums worldwide
facts.lifespan: Short — many live less than 2 years
facts.food: Mostly algae, plus tiny animals and insects

entries.definition: Members of the genus Lophius, commonly called monkfish, toadfish, sea frogs, fishing frogs, frogfish, and sea devils, are various species of lophiid anglerfishes found in the Atlantic and Indian Oceans.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Lophius”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Monkfish (genus Lophius)
facts.habitat: Seabeds of the Atlantic and other seas
facts.food: Fish, lured close by a fleshy lure on its head

entries.definition: Moray eels, or Muraenidae, are a family of eels whose members are found worldwide.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Moray eel”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Moray eels (family Muraenidae)
facts.habitat: Warm seas worldwide, in reef holes and crevices
facts.food: Fish, octopus and crabs

entries.definition: The mullets or grey mullets are a family (Mugilidae) of ray-finned fish found worldwide in coastal temperate and tropical waters, and some species in fresh water.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Mullet (fish)”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Grey mullets (family Mugilidae)
facts.habitat: Warm and temperate coasts and river mouths worldwide
facts.food: Algae and bits of food sifted from mud

entries.definition: Needlefish (family Belonidae) or long toms are piscivorous fishes primarily associated with very shallow marine habitats or the surface of the open sea.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Needlefish”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Needlefish (family Belonidae)
facts.habitat: Shallow warm seas; a few live in rivers
facts.food: Small fish

entries.definition: Oarfish are the three species of large and extremely long pelagic lampriform fish belonging to the small family Regalecidae.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Oarfish”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Giant oarfish (Regalecus glesne)
facts.habitat: The deep open ocean worldwide
facts.food: Krill, small fish and squid
facts.size: Up to 8 m — the longest bony fish

entries.definition: The opah, also commonly known as moonfish, sunfish (not to be confused with Molidae or ocean sunfish), cowfish, kingfish, and redfin ocean pan are large, colorful, deep-bodied pelagic lampriform fishes comprising the genus Lampris, of the small family Lampridae (also spelled Lamprididae).
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Opah”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Opah (genus Lampris)
facts.habitat: Open seas worldwide, in deep water
facts.food: Squid, krill and small fish

entries.definition: Pacu is a common name used to refer to several species of omnivorous South American freshwater serrasalmid fish related to piranhas.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Pacu”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Pacu (several kinds, related to piranhas)
facts.habitat: Rivers of South America, especially the Amazon
facts.food: Fruit, seeds and nuts that fall into the water, crushed with human-like teeth

entries.definition: Parrotfish (named because their mouths resemble a parrot's beak) are a clade of fish placed in the subfamily Scarinae of the wrasse family (Labridae).
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Parrotfish”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Parrotfish (subfamily Scarinae)
facts.habitat: Warm coral reefs worldwide
facts.food: Algae scraped off coral with a beak-like mouth
facts.size: Up to 1.3 m, most around 50 cm

entries.definition: Perch is a common name for freshwater fish from the genus Perca, which belongs to the family Percidae of the large order Perciformes.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Perch”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: European perch (Perca fluviatilis)
facts.habitat: Lakes and rivers in Europe and Asia
facts.food: Insects, small fish and shrimp
facts.size: Up to 60 cm, usually around 25 cm

entries.definition: The northern pike (Esox lucius), also known as jack, northern or simply pike, is a species of carnivorous fish of the genus Esox (pikes).
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Northern pike”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Northern pike (Esox lucius)
facts.habitat: Weedy lakes and rivers in the cool north of the world
facts.food: Mostly fish, sometimes frogs and crayfish, ambushed from weeds

entries.definition: A piranha is any of a number of freshwater fish species in the subfamily Serrasalminae, of the family Serrasalmidae, in the order Characiformes.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Piranha”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Red-bellied piranha (Pygocentrus nattereri)
facts.habitat: Rivers of South America
facts.food: Insects, worms and fish
facts.size: Up to 50 cm, most under 35 cm

entries.definition: Plaice is a common name for a group of flatfish that comprises four species: the European, American, Alaskan and scale-eye plaice.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Plaice”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: European plaice (Pleuronectes platessa)
facts.habitat: Sandy seabeds of the northeast Atlantic
facts.food: Shellfish and worms
facts.size: Up to 1 m, usually around 40 cm

entries.definition: Platy is a common name of freshwater fish in the genus Xiphophorus that lack a "sword" at the bottom of their tails.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Platy (fish)”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Southern platyfish (Xiphophorus maculatus)
facts.habitat: Warm streams in Mexico and Central America; aquariums worldwide
facts.food: Worms, small crustaceans, insects and plants

entries.definition: Pollock or pollack (pronounced ) is the common name used for either of the two species of North Atlantic marine fish in the genus Pollachius.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Pollock”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Atlantic pollock (Pollachius pollachius)
facts.habitat: Rocky coasts of the northeast Atlantic
facts.food: Not well known

entries.definition: Pompanos are marine fish in the genus Trachinotus in the subfamily Trachinotinae in the family Trachinotidae.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Pompano”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Florida pompano (Trachinotus carolinus)
facts.habitat: Sandy beaches and surf of the western Atlantic
facts.food: Clams, crabs and other small animals, and small fish

entries.definition: Sparidae, the seabreams and porgies, is a family of ray-finned fishes belonging to the order Acanthuriformes, although they were previously classified in the order Perciformes.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Sparidae”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Porgies and sea breams (family Sparidae)
facts.habitat: Warm and temperate coasts worldwide
facts.food: Crabs, clams, sea urchins and worms
facts.size: Up to 2 m, most around 40 cm

entries.definition: Tetraodontidae is a family of marine and freshwater fish in the order Tetraodontiformes.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Tetraodontidae”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Pufferfish (family Tetraodontidae)
facts.habitat: Warm seas worldwide; some in rivers
facts.food: Algae and small shellfish and crabs, crushed with beak-like teeth

entries.definition: The rainbow trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss) is a species of trout native to cold-water tributaries of the Pacific Ocean in North America and Asia.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Rainbow trout”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Rainbow trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss)
facts.habitat: Cool rivers and lakes; native to the Pacific side of North America
facts.food: Insects and other small creatures, and small fish

entries.definition: The red drum (Sciaenops ocellatus), also known as redfish, channel bass, puppy drum, spottail bass, or simply red, is a game fish found in the Atlantic Ocean from Massachusetts to Florida and in the Gulf of Mexico from Florida to northern Mexico.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Red drum”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Red drum (Sciaenops ocellatus)
facts.habitat: Coasts and river mouths of the western Atlantic and Gulf of Mexico
facts.food: Crabs, shrimp and fish

entries.definition: The roach, or rutilus roach (Rutilus rutilus), also known as the common roach, is a fresh- and brackish-water fish of the family Cyprinidae, native to most of Europe and western Asia.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Common roach”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Common roach (Rutilus rutilus)
facts.habitat: Lakes and rivers across Europe and western Asia
facts.food: Insects, snails and water plants
facts.size: Up to 50 cm, usually under 35 cm

entries.definition: The sablefish (Anoplopoma fimbria) is one of two members of the fish family Anoplopomatidae and the only species in the genus Anoplopoma.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Sablefish”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Sablefish (Anoplopoma fimbria)
facts.habitat: Deep muddy seabeds of the North Pacific
facts.food: Fish, squid and krill

entries.definition: The sailfish is one or two species of marine fish in the genus Istiophorus, which belong to the family Istiophoridae (marlins).
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Sailfish”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Sailfish (genus Istiophorus)
facts.habitat: Warm open seas worldwide
facts.food: Fish and squid
facts.size: Up to 3.5 m — one of the fastest fish

entries.definition: Salmon are any of several commercially important species of euryhaline ray-finned fish from the genera Salmo and Oncorhynchus of the family Salmonidae, native to tributaries of the North Atlantic (Salmo) and North Pacific (Oncorhynchus) basins.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Salmon”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar)
facts.habitat: Born in rivers, grows up at sea, and comes back to its river to breed
facts.food: Insects in rivers; fish and shrimp at sea

entries.definition: Sardine and pilchard are common names for various species of small, oily forage fish in the herring suborder Clupeoidei.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Sardine”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: European pilchard (Sardina pilchardus)
facts.habitat: Coastal seas of the northeast Atlantic and the Mediterranean, in big schools
facts.food: Plankton

entries.definition: The Atlantic horse mackerel (Trachurus trachurus), also known as the European horse mackerel or common scad, is a species of jack mackerel in the family Carangidae, which includes the jacks, pompanos and trevallies.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Atlantic horse mackerel”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Atlantic horse mackerel (Trachurus trachurus)
facts.habitat: Coastal seas of the eastern Atlantic and the Mediterranean
facts.food: Small fish, shrimp and squid
facts.size: Up to 60 cm, usually around 25 cm

entries.definition: A seahorse (also written sea-horse and sea horse) is any of 47 species of small marine bony fish in the genus Hippocampus.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Seahorse”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Seahorses (genus Hippocampus)
facts.habitat: Shallow warm seas, among seagrass and coral
facts.food: Food sucked in through a long snout — they must eat almost all the time

entries.definition: The Alosidae, or the shads, are a family of clupeiform fishes.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Alosidae”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Shads (family Alosidae)
facts.habitat: Varies between kinds
facts.food: Varies between kinds

entries.definition: Sharks are a group of elasmobranch cartilaginous fishes characterized by a ribless endoskeleton, dermal denticles, five to seven gill slits on each side, and pectoral fins that are not fused to the head.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Shark”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Sharks (superorder Selachimorpha)
facts.habitat: Every ocean, from the shore to the deep sea
facts.food: Fish, seals, squid or plankton, depending on the kind

entries.definition: The silver carp or silverfin (Hypophthalmichthys molitrix) is a species of freshwater cyprinid fish, a variety of Asian carp native to China and eastern Siberia, from the Amur River drainage in the north to the Xi Jiang River drainage in the south.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Silver carp”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Silver carp (Hypophthalmichthys molitrix)
facts.habitat: Big rivers; native to East Asia, invasive in North America
facts.food: Plankton
facts.size: Up to 1.4 m — and it leaps out of the water when startled

entries.definition: Skates are cartilaginous fish belonging to the family Rajidae in the superorder Batoidea of rays.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Skate (fish)”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Skates (family Rajidae)
facts.habitat: Seabeds worldwide, from the shallows to the deep sea
facts.food: Shrimp, crabs, clams and other seabed animals

entries.definition: Lutjanidae, the snappers and fusiliers, are a family of percomorph fishes, mainly marine but with some members inhabiting estuaries and, in some cases, fresh water (e.g., Lutjanus goldiei).
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Lutjanidae”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Snappers (family Lutjanidae)
facts.habitat: Warm seas worldwide, around reefs
facts.food: Fish, crabs and shrimp
facts.size: Up to 1.5 m, most under 1 m

entries.definition: The sockeye salmon (Oncorhynchus nerka), also called red salmon, kokanee salmon, blueback salmon, or simply sockeye, is an anadromous species of salmon found in the Northern Pacific Ocean and rivers discharging into it.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Sockeye salmon”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Sockeye salmon (Oncorhynchus nerka)
facts.habitat: The North Pacific and the rivers and lakes around it, turning bright red to breed
facts.food: Mostly plankton

entries.definition: A sole is a fish belonging to several families in the suborder Pleuronectoidei.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Sole (fish)”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Common sole (Solea solea)
facts.habitat: Sandy seabeds of the northeast Atlantic and Mediterranean
facts.food: Worms, shellfish and small crustaceans, hunted at night

entries.definition: Ephippidae is a family of percomorph fishes in the suborder Moronoidei of the order Acanthuriformes.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Ephippidae”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Spadefish (family Ephippidae)
facts.habitat: Warm coasts and reefs worldwide
facts.food: Algae, sponges, worms and other small seabed animals

entries.definition: Sprat is the common name applied to a group of forage fish belonging to the genus Sprattus in the family Clupeidae.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Sprat”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: European sprat (Sprattus sprattus)
facts.habitat: Coastal seas of Europe, in big schools
facts.food: Plankton
facts.size: Up to 25 cm, usually around 12 cm

entries.definition: The sticklebacks are a family of ray-finned fishes, the Gasterosteidae which have a Holarctic distribution in fresh, brackish and marine waters.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Stickleback”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Three-spined stickleback (Gasterosteus aculeatus)
facts.habitat: Ponds, streams and coasts in the north of the world
facts.food: Insects, worms and tiny crustaceans
facts.size: Up to 11 cm, usually around 5 cm

entries.definition: Stingrays are a group of rays, a type of cartilaginous fish.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Stingray”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Stingrays (order Myliobatiformes)
facts.habitat: Warm shallow seas worldwide; some in rivers
facts.food: Clams, shrimp, crabs and worms dug from the sand

entries.definition: Sturgeon are the 27 species of fish belonging to the family Acipenseridae.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Sturgeon”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Sturgeons (family Acipenseridae)
facts.habitat: Rivers, lakes and coasts in the north of the world
facts.food: Snails, worms, shellfish and small fish from the bottom
facts.size: Up to 7 m in the beluga

entries.definition: The remora, sometimes called suckerfish or sharksucker, is any of a family (Echeneidae) of ray-finned fish in the order Carangiformes.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Remora”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Remoras (family Echeneidae)
facts.habitat: Warm open seas, riding on sharks, whales and turtles
facts.food: Scraps from their host's meals

entries.definition: The ocean sunfish (Mola mola), also known as the common mola, is one of the largest ray-finned fish in the world.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Ocean sunfish”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Ocean sunfish (Mola mola)
facts.habitat: Warm and temperate open seas worldwide
facts.lifespan: Not known for sure — perhaps over 20 years
facts.food: Jellyfish, small fish, molluscs and other small sea animals
facts.size: Up to 3.3 m and 1.3 tonnes — one of the heaviest bony fish

entries.definition: The swordfish (Xiphias gladius), also known as the broadbill in some countries, are large, highly migratory predatory fish characterized by a long, flat, sword-like, pointed bill.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Swordfish”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Swordfish (Xiphias gladius)
facts.habitat: Open seas worldwide
facts.food: Fish and squid, slashed with its long flat bill

entries.definition: The Acanthuridae are a family of ray-finned fishes, which includes surgeonfishes, tangs, and unicornfishes.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Acanthuridae”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Tangs and surgeonfish (family Acanthuridae)
facts.habitat: Warm coral reefs worldwide
facts.food: Algae
facts.size: Up to 1 m, most around 25 cm

entries.definition: The tench or doctor fish (Tinca tinca) is a fresh- and brackish-water fish of the order Cypriniformes found throughout Eurasia from Western Europe including Britain and Ireland east into Asia as far as the Ob and Yenisei Rivers.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Tench”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Tench (Tinca tinca)
facts.habitat: Weedy lakes, ponds and slow rivers across Europe and western Asia
facts.food: Small animals from the bottom, especially snails and tiny clams, and plants

entries.definition: Tetra is the common name of many small freshwater characiform fishes.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Tetra”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Tetras (several families of small characins)
facts.habitat: Rivers and streams of South America and Africa; aquariums worldwide
facts.food: Varies between kinds

entries.definition: Hydrocynus is a genus of Characin fish in the family Alestidae commonly called "tigerfish," native to Africa.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Hydrocynus”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: African tigerfish (genus Hydrocynus)
facts.habitat: Rivers and lakes across Africa
facts.food: Fish, and even birds snatched in flight

entries.definition: Tilapia ( tih-LAH-pee-ə) is the common name for nearly a hundred species of cichlid fish from the coelotilapine, coptodonine, heterotilapine, oreochromine, pelmatolapiine, and tilapiine tribes (formerly all were "Tilapiini"), with the economically most important species placed in the Coptodonini and Oreochromini.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Tilapia”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Tilapia (many kinds of cichlid)
facts.habitat: Warm lakes and rivers; native to Africa and the Middle East, farmed worldwide
facts.food: Algae, plants and small creatures

entries.definition: Triggerfish are one of 41 species of marine, ray-finned fishes belonging to the family Balistidae.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Triggerfish”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Triggerfish (family Balistidae)
facts.habitat: Warm coral reefs worldwide
facts.food: Varies between kinds
facts.size: Up to 1 m, most around 30 cm

entries.definition: Trout is a generic common name for numerous species of carnivorous freshwater fishes belonging to the genera Oncorhynchus, Salmo, and Salvelinus, all of which are members of the subfamily Salmoninae in the family Salmonidae.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Trout”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Brown trout (Salmo trutta)
facts.habitat: Cool, clean rivers and lakes; native to Europe
facts.food: Insects, shrimp and small fish
facts.size: Up to 1.4 m, usually under 75 cm

entries.definition: Tuna (pl.: tunas or tuna) are saltwater fish belonging to the tribe Thunnini, a subgrouping of the Scombridae (mackerel) family.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Tuna”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Tuna (tribe Thunnini)
facts.habitat: Open seas worldwide
facts.food: Other sea animals — tuna are fast hunters

entries.definition: The turbot, Scophthalmus maximus, is a relatively large species of flatfish in the family Scophthalmidae.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Turbot”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Turbot (Scophthalmus maximus)
facts.habitat: Sandy seabeds of the northeast Atlantic, the Baltic and the Mediterranean
facts.food: Mostly other bottom fish, plus crabs and shellfish

entries.definition: A viperfish is any species of the genus Chauliodus, marine fish inhabiting the twilight or mesopelagic zone.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Viperfish”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Viperfish (genus Chauliodus)
facts.habitat: The deep, dark ocean worldwide
facts.food: Fish and shrimp, drawn in by a glowing lure and caught with needle-like teeth

entries.definition: The whale shark (Rhincodon typus) is a slow-moving, filter-feeding carpet shark and the largest known extant fish species.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Whale shark”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Whale shark (Rhincodon typus)
facts.habitat: Warm open seas worldwide
facts.food: Plankton and small fish, filtered from the water
facts.size: Up to about 18 m — the biggest fish in the world

entries.definition: Merlangius merlangus, commonly known as whiting or merling, is an important food fish in the eastern North Atlantic Ocean and the northern Mediterranean, western Baltic, and Black Sea.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Merlangius”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Whiting (Merlangius merlangus)
facts.habitat: Coastal seas of the northeast Atlantic
facts.food: Shrimp, crabs and small fish
facts.size: Up to 90 cm, usually around 25 cm

entries.definition: The wrasses are a family, Labridae, of marine ray-finned fish, many of which are brightly colored.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Wrasse”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Wrasses (family Labridae)
facts.habitat: Reefs and rocky coasts worldwide
facts.food: Small creatures, and some clean parasites off other fish
facts.size: From 5 cm to 2.5 m, most under 20 cm

entries.definition: The Japanese amberjack or yellowtail, Seriola quinqueradiata, is a species of jack fish in the family Carangidae, native to the northwest Pacific Ocean.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Japanese amberjack”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Japanese amberjack (Seriola quinqueradiata)
facts.habitat: Coastal seas of the northwest Pacific
facts.food: Plankton

entries.definition: The zander (Sander lucioperca), sander, pikeperch, or Eurasian pikeperch, is a species of ray-finned fish from the family Percidae (which also includes perch, ruffe and darter).
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Zander”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Zander (Sander lucioperca)
facts.habitat: Lakes and slow, murky rivers across Europe and western Asia
facts.food: Fish
facts.size: Up to 1 m, usually around 50 cm

entries.definition: The zebrafish (Danio rerio) is a species of danionin belonging to the genus Danio in the suborder Cyprinoidei.
entries.credit: From the Wikipedia article “Zebrafish”, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.name: Zebrafish (Danio rerio)
facts.habitat: Streams, ponds and rice paddies of South Asia; aquariums and laboratories worldwide
facts.food: Worms, small crustaceans and insect larvae
